messages.author: d3e2e3c09c385ed8
messages.subject: Re: Plot 3 lines in one graph
parts:
I found a method to do what I wanted :-)

y<-reshape(x, varying = c("FT", "PT", "NW"), 
           v.names = "Value", timevar = "h", 
           times = c("FT", "PT", "NW"), 
           new.row.names = 1:1000, 
           direction = "long")

if there is a better way of doing it please let me know.

Thanks!

print(x)
     V1       V2       V3      V4

2 -2800 15195.73 5415.219 7264.28
x$V1 Is the vector of coordinates for the horizontal axis and V2, V3, V4 the vectors for the vertical.

     id       x       y

parts:
Yes. Use melt() from the reshape package.

 

melt(x, id.var = “h”, measure.var = c(“FT”, “PT”, “NW”))

 

or if x contains only those 4 variables

 

melt(x, id.var = “h”)

<- melt( d, id.vars=c("id","x") ) and (2) plot it, qplot( x, value,

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Plot 3 lines in one graph
parts:
Hi:

Here's what I think Ben meant in terms of the toy example (rewritten with cleaner code):

V <- data.frame( time = seq(30), var1 = rnorm(30),
                  var2 = rnorm(30) + 3, var3 = rnorm(30) + 6)
library('reshape2')

# Reshape V from 'wide' form to 'long' form
Vm <- melt(V, id = "time")
str(Vm)
levels(Vm$variable)
head(Vm)

# This form is convenient for ggplot() because now the
# variables Var1-Var3 can be accessed as a single entity:

ggplot(Vm, aes(x = time, y = value, color = variable)) +
    geom_line() +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-2, 8)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("red", "blue", "black"))

You can create a factor on the fly, but it is not immediately obvious how to do so; fortunately, Hadley provided an example in the ggplot2 book. The idea is to put the aesthetic to be created in aes() and sequentially augment its set of values with multiple calls to the geom. You can then use the appropriate scale_* function to fine tune the legend guide.

ggplot(V, aes(x = time)) +
   geom_line(aes(y = var1, color = "var1")) +
   geom_line(aes(y = var2, color = "var2")) +
   geom_line(aes(y = var3, color = "var3")) +
   coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-2, 8)) +
   labs(color = "Variable") +
   scale_color_manual(values = c("red", "blue", "black"))

Is that what you were asking about?

Dennis
